newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss chocolate sales fall in 1996, exports stall.
newsitem.headline: Swiss chocolate sales fall in 1996, exports stall.

text.p: Swiss chocolate sales fell slightly last year, while exports stalled for the first time in over a decade, industry association Chocosuisse said.
"Steady, strong growth in exports which has been seen for over 10 years came to a halt in 1996," Chocosuisse said.
But it expected 1997 to show improvements "thanks to enhanced competitiveness linked to currency factors" following the recent weakening in the Swiss franc.

The Swiss per capita consumption of chocolate also rose slightly to 10.9 kilograms in 1996 from 10.7 in 1995. The increase was tied to a cool summer, a large number of new products and a "certain pent-up demand," Chocosuisse said.
Total sales were 128,229 tonnes in 1996, down from 128,270 tonnes in 1995. In value terms, total sales fell to 1.152 billion Swiss francs in 1996 from 1.168 billion in 1995.
The figures include imports and exports and sales of products containing chocolate. Exports to over 100 countries, remained at roughly 47 percent of total sales volume.
In value terms, exports amounted to 378 million Swiss francs, down from 392 million in 1995.
In volume terms, 60,434 tonnes were exported in 1996 compared with 60,756 tonnes reported last year.
Domestic sales showed slight growth, despite a weak economy, Chocosuisse said.
The 16 Swiss chocolate producers were even able to slightly increase their sales to 67,795 tonnes, compared with 67,451 tonnes in 1995.
In Swiss franc terms, the value of domestic sales fell slightly by 0.3 percent to 774 million francs from 776 million francs in the past year.
Exporters' share in Switzerland's domestic market rose to 18.1 percent from 17.9 percent, Chocosuisse said. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
